items.body_html: a process gate executes with cwd = runtime_context workspace (v1: the worktree); a workflow declaring runtime_context: none may not bind an external.process gate — the static mismatch is a definition error, and the kernel also guards it at run with Rejected(runtime_context_required_for_process_gate)

items.name_html: gate config validated at definition load
items.body_html: validate_gate_config(raw) is the external.process registration's validate_and_normalize_config body, run by ADMISSION (admit_definition) at definition load: a process gate without a workspace (runtime_context_required_for_process_gate — via the registration's requires_runtime_context flag), a fail_instance disposition (gate_config_not_supported), or an incomplete/invalid config — missing command / timeout_ms, an unknown output.mode or runner disposition, or exit_code buckets that are missing or not allow | warn | block (invalid_process_gate_config) — is a DEFINITION ISSUE at admission, never a mid-run surprise; the HANDLE ready(∅) lane keeps the runtime backstop. Defaults (output.mode, dispositions) MATERIALIZE into the effective config — resolved once, downstream reads one form
every process gate carries a timeout_ms; a timeout is a runner outcome, not an indefinite block (v1 had none)
a log + artifact is persisted whether the gate allows, warns, or blocks (v1-faithful); the ref is carried to the commit or the rejection
verdict source is exit_code or gate_decision_json by config — never guessed from whether stdout happens to parse
runner_error / timeout / malformed_gate_decision_json → block_transition with a distinct reason, separable in audit from a test_failed block
a deferred process gate is still rejected (gate_execution_not_supported) — the deferred lifecycle is a later slice
